text:
maria: heads up — production started seeing 502s to our inference proxy in eu-west-1 around 08:42 UTC, looks like TLS handshake failures at the ALB layer
jon: saw that, noticed the SNI on a few failed connections is blank. health-checks? or something rewriting Host header?
infra-bot: ALB(ingress-prod-eu) reported: "TLS handshake failure: no certificate matched SNI" x17 over last 10m
alex: interesting — our nginx ingress was recently updated to rewrite `Host` for internal backends (configmap change last night). Could that strip SNI on HTTP/1.0 probes?
kevin: SNI is in TLS ClientHello, Host header is HTTP-level. In theory Host rewrite shouldn't affect SNI. But I have seen ALBs choose the "default" listener cert when they get an empty SNI (e.g., certain health probes or when client doesn't set server_name).
maria: reproducing locally: `openssl s_client -connect alb-eu:443 -servername '' -tlsextdebug` shows ALB serving the wildcard cert for the listener default, not the route-specific cert. so backend routing is fine, but cert mismatch causes some clients to fail earlier
jon: do we have multiple certs attached to same listener with host-based rules? I thought we used cert-per-host-rule on the ALB listeners but maybe we relied on ALB's SNI routing by ordering
alex: ALB docs: when multiple rules/certs exist, ALB uses SNI to pick certificate bound to rule. If SNI missing, it falls back to the default certificate for the listener (first in list). If that default doesn't match the client's expected name, clients fail.
kevin: this matches error pattern: legacy health probes and some older HTTP/1.0 clients don't set SNI. Also our internal probe (kube-probe) runs TLS client without server_name by accident because of a library upgrade last week.
maria: timeline: kube-probe update rolled 08:35 -> first errors 08:42. coincidence unlikely
jon: proposed fixes: 1) make the listener default cert be a SAN cert covering all prod hosts (short term), 2) patch kube-probe to send proper SNI (medium), 3) update ingress to ensure ALB gets explicit host header via target group health checks (longer). Which order?
alex: can do (2) quickly — change probe container to use `--tls-servername=${HOST}` env and roll a patch. But that only helps kube-probe. For external clients we should avoid relying on default fallback cert, so (1) is safest immediate mitigation.
kevin: I can generate a multi-SAN cert (let's reuse our internal CA) and replace listener default tonight. low blast radius. Will need a short maintenance window for cert swap? ALB cert replace is hot, no restart.
maria: also let's add a guard: detect incoming TLS connections with no SNI and log counts per host so we can see offenders. ALB logs have `sni` field?
infra-bot: ALB access logs show `tls_sni` when available, else `-`. Filtering shows ~1200 requests with `-` in last hour, source IPs include our kube nodes + some external clients.
jon: while you change the default cert, alex please prepare a probe patch and a small rollout plan (canary to eu-west-1 staging then prod). kevin, coordinate cert rotation with infra oncall.
alex: will do. patch ready in a few mins, can push to canary traffic by 09:20 UTC.
kevin: generating SAN cert now. planning to attach to listener as default by 09:05 UTC, then monitor metrics for 15m.
maria: quick test commands for reproducibility if someone needs to verify behavior locally:
```
# missing SNI -> ALB serves default cert
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu.example.net:443 -servername '' -showcerts
# set SNI -> expected host cert
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu.example.net:443 -servername api.prod.example.net -showcerts
```
jon: also add this to the postmortem: don't rely on ALB default cert ordering for SNI missing cases, we need explicit default cert that is permissive.
alex: rolling probe patch to canary now. I'll ping thread when canary passes.
kevin: attached cert; swapping default in 5. will monitor for TLS handshake errors in ALB metrics+CloudWatch.
maria: thanks — keeping this thread as the coordination point. If anyone sees unexplained client errors after 09:30 UTC, drop them here. :eyes:
